verdicts.evidence: 8 runs on n=8, d=3 MRPs show fixed-point spread 0.0284 and distance to analytic θ* 0.0497; η-sweep (0.110→0.0185) gives log-log exponent −1.64 (R²=0.991), consistent with Õ(ε⁻¹η⁻²); mutation reusing the same sample yields distance 1.071, confirming the independence mechanism.
Markov sampling with slowed mixing (gap=0.6) gives exponent −1.67 (R²=0.992), matching the i.i.d. rate; fixed-point distance 0.0665; coupled-chain mutation yields distance 1.774.

Dimension sweep d=2…32 (n=64) with decaying stepsizes shows flat normalized error (d-exponent 0.285); mutation dropping the normalization assumption gives d-exponent 5.65 with divergence at d=32, confirming the assumption is load-bearing.

Double-chain exponents −1.64/−1.67 (quadratic) vs single-chain −3.76 (quartic), gap ≈2 in the exponent; however, prior-work algorithms [11,17,21] were not re-implemented and the discounted-TD matching uses a proxy η_disc, so the literature-attribution part is not independently checked.

Single-chain exponent −3.76 (R²=0.994) vs double-chain −1.91 (R²=0.996), gap 1.85, close to predicted −4 vs −2; the only structural change is replacing the independent second chain with a running average, and the exponent degrades by ~2 as the theorem predicts.

300 random instances (n∈[4,20), d∈[1,8)) with 0 violations of η₁ ≥ ½η₃ (min ratio 1.042); dropping the (μᵀΦx)² correction term causes 200/200 violations; Dirichlet identity verified numerically to 8.9e-16.

overall: The logbook provides real experimental evidence on randomly generated MRPs supporting all six claims, including sample-complexity scaling exponents consistent with theory, fixed-point convergence checks, dimension-independence tests, and numerical lemma verification with mutation tests confirming mechanisms. Main limitations are small problem sizes (n=8–64), limited η-sweep ranges (4–6×), and the absence of prior-work re-implementation for the comparative claims in Claim 4.
